sections.name: File setup, source
sections.title: Imports and a sample area reading helper
sections.what: Brings in the test tools, the comparison functions and a helper that builds a labelled area reading for a given source type.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small helper keeps each test short and readable.

sections.name: parcel area normalization
sections.title: Unit conversion checks
sections.what: Checks that acre, hectare and square metre readings convert to acres correctly. Checks that unsupported units, text numbers, non-numbers, zero and negative values give nothing rather than a guess.
sections.why: Likely reason: a wrong conversion would create a false area discrepancy, so only known units are accepted.

sections.name: parcel area comparison policy
sections.title: Comparison status and summary checks
sections.what: Checks the exact cut-off points that decide consistent, review and potential issue, that the percentage is the same in both directions, that missing data gives insufficient evidence, and that the hero, control and missing-source summaries come out as expected.
sections.why: Likely reason: the demo verdict depends on these exact cut-offs, so tests pin them down.
sections.watch_out: The boundary values are fixed in these tests, so changing a threshold means updating these expectations too.

summary: Tests how areas are converted to acres and how two area readings are compared, including exact threshold edges and the overall summary.
purpose: Checks the acre conversion rules, the percentage cut-offs (consistent, review, potential issue) and the handling of missing data.
why: Likely reason: the comparison result is a demo verdict, so its edge cases are pinned down by tests.
how: Section one imports the functions and a helper that builds a labelled area reading. Section two checks conversion to acres for accepted units and rejects bad or unsupported values. Section three checks threshold edges, the symmetry of the percentage, missing data, and the hero, control and missing-source summaries.
inputs: Sample area readings with values and units.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Passing these tests does not make the tolerances legally valid. The code itself says they are demo values.
debug: If a status changes at an edge, compare with the threshold values in the parcel area comparison service.
